confirm.reason: The bank point e-equilibrium covers equilibrium and how shortages and surpluses move the price, but it also teaches demand and supply shifts and simultaneous shifts, with a question on a double shift, so it is broader than this brief.

draft.title: Market equilibrium
card: Market equilibrium is the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. At this price, buyers want to buy exactly what sellers want to sell.
the price is below equilibrium, so quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied. Buyers compete for the limited goods, which pushes the price up.
the price is above equilibrium, so quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded. Sellers are left with unsold goods and cut prices, which pushes the price down.
Prices keep moving until the shortage or surplus is gone. The market then settles at the equilibrium price and quantity.
draft.remember: Shortage: price rises. Surplus: price falls. Both end at equilibrium.

a.q: A market has a surplus. Which statement describes it?
opts: Quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded
Quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied
Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
The price is below the equilibrium price
a.why: A surplus means sellers offer more than buyers want at the current price, so supply is greater than demand. The option about demand being greater describes a shortage, which is the reverse.
a.clue: Think about who is left with goods they cannot sell.

b.q: Mia sells fresh mangoes at a market stall in Mildura. At $4 each, she has 80 mangoes left over at the end of the day. What is most likely to happen to the price if the market keeps adjusting?
opts: It falls, because $4 is above the equilibrium price
It rises, because $4 is below the equilibrium price
It stays at $4, because Mia sets the price
It rises, because there are goods left to sell
b.why: Unsold mangoes mean quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded at $4, which is a surplus. A surplus shows the price is above equilibrium, so sellers cut prices until it clears. Leftover goods do not push prices up.
b.clue: Leftover stock means sellers offered more than buyers wanted.

a.best: Quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded

b.best: It falls, because $4 is above the equilibrium price

problems.detail: The why says a surplus means 'supply is greater than demand'. That blurs the card's terms: supply and demand are whole curves, and a surplus means quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded. VCE students are taught to keep these apart (movement along a curve versus a shift), so the why should say 'quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded'.

check.summary: Both questions are correct and each has one right answer. The only problem is that the why for (a) says 'supply is greater than demand' instead of 'quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded', which blurs a distinction the chapter relies on.
